walkthroughs.body_html:
Lunar Disc & Eclipses — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lunar Disc & Eclipses brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Full Moon”?
options: Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Last quarter”?
options: Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Waxing / waning”?
options: Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “New Moon”?
options: Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.
Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Synodic month”?
options: Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.
Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “First quarter”?
options: Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.
